name: ilang
description: iLang, the native language of AI: the official runtime, the canon validator, dictionary and FAQ lookup, SOUL 2.0 and Source Book 2.9, from mcp.ilang.ai/mcp.

interface.longDescription: Gives the model the official iLang through read-only MCP tools: the runtime (checked against the canon's sha256) or its syntax and vocabulary alone, any section of the full text, the canon grammar validator, lookup over the dictionary and the ilang.ai FAQ, and the two published iLang documents, SOUL 2.0 and Source Book 2.9, with version, DOI and sha256. With the Source Book, the model can turn a tutorial into BOOK.md, an iLang engineering book, and check it with ilang_book_check. No API key.
defaultPrompt: Load the iLang runtime, then write an iLang engineering book from this tutorial and check it

positive.prompt: Load the iLang runtime and tell me which runtime version you loaded.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls ilang_runtime. The reply names the runtime version from the <ilang-runtime version=...> tag, for example 2026.10.31-6f17c3d64219.

positive.description: Validate iLang and suggest the right modifier
positive.prompt: Check this iLang line and fix it: [XLAT:@USER|src=en|tgt=zh]=>[Ω]
positive.expected_behavior: Calls ilang_validate. Reports one error, E302 for the modifier tgt, with did_you_mean lng, and gives a corrected line that uses lng=zh and validates with zero errors.

positive.description: Look up a verb in the iLang dictionary
positive.prompt: In iLang, what does the verb XLAT do, and what is its Greek alias?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls ilang_lookup with XLAT. Answers: a Transform verb that translates between languages, alias θ, with the dictionary link https://ilang.ai/dictionary/ .

positive.prompt: Give me the iLang SOUL 2.0 document with its DOI.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls ilang_soul. The reply gives version 2.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23778215, the sha256 9b22c7d5bbbcbca24db044cb5c9d2bb98b8e019b776a764e339b505d465a66f1 and the document text returned by the tool.

positive.prompt:
Run the iLang book check on this engineering book:
::ILANG::v5.0::ENGINEERING_BOOK
[READ:@LOCAL|path=README.md]=>[SHRT|len=short]=>[Ω]
::ILANG::v5.0::ENGINEERING_BOOK
positive.expected_behavior: Calls ilang_book_check with the full text. Reports pass true: A1 found 2 markers, A2 zero errors and zero warnings.

negative.description: Plain translation request; iLang has a translate verb, but the user only wants a translation
negative.prompt: Translate this into Chinese: The meeting has moved to Friday.

negative.description: General code validation; ilang_validate checks only iLang text
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that validates an email address.

negative.description: English word definition; ilang_lookup covers only iLang terms
negative.prompt: What does the word serendipity mean?

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: nine read-only tools from mcp.ilang.ai/mcp (the iLang runtime and its lite form, sections of the full text, the canon grammar validator with modifier suggestions, dictionary and FAQ lookup, SOUL 2.0, Source Book 2.9 and the engineering book check), plus a skill that tells the model when to use them. No API key.
